hyps.why: Very small learning rates leave Adam undertrained within 243 epochs, so increasing them yields large gains.
Learning rates near 0.28-1 cause divergence, so increasing further hurts accuracy.
Reducing an overly large learning rate restores stable training.
Large batches give less noisy gradients and fewer updates, so they benefit from larger steps.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise that destabilizes high-learning-rate training.
With a low learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and stronger undertraining.
Smaller batches give more updates per epoch, compensating for tiny step sizes.
Near alpha=1 additional L2 penalty causes severe underfitting, whereas at tiny alphas it is negligible.
Deeper ReLU nets are more prone to divergence and dead units at large learning rates.
Widening very narrow networks removes a capacity bottleneck, while wide nets see diminishing returns.
